group_assessment.weighting: A Chinese cardiovascular-genetics group (Guangxi Medical University, from the affiliations) with a series of lipid-SNP interaction papers. Primary for its own cohort; not primary for WWOX or WWOX disease. Observations (genotype counts) weighed above interpretation (gene-gene and gene-environment models, mechanism sentences); the interpretation sentences cite sources that do not match their reference entries.

entries.proposition: Design: three hospital-based groups (CAD 622, ischemic stroke 593, controls 638) from one Chinese hospital, Han, unrelated; controls are described as normal subjects without CAD or stroke; this is a case-control association study of common SNPs, not a loss-of-function cohort.
entries.snippet: A total of 638 normal subjects without a history of CAD and IS were used as a control group.

entries.proposition: SNPs were selected from earlier lipid GWAS and restricted to MAF above 10 percent; WWOX is represented by two common SNPs, rs2222896 and rs2278075.
entries.snippet: SNPs with minor allele frequencies (MAFs) > 10% were included.

entries.proposition: Genotype counts for the WWOX SNP rs2278075 by group: T allele 15 percent in controls, 21 percent in CAD, 23 percent in stroke.
rs2278075 is the only WWOX SNP whose CAD and stroke associations pass the paper's Bonferroni line in Table 3 (dominant model OR 1.63 for CAD and 1.81 for stroke).
The paper's Bonferroni significance line for Table 3 is P below 0.00021.
entries.snippet: The PCAD or PIS < 0.00021 was considered statistical significance after the Bonferroni correction (6 SNPs × 5 models × 8 factors).

entries.proposition: The other WWOX SNP, rs2222896, does not pass that line for stroke (dominant OR 0.71, P 0.0025).
The text says all six SNPs, in three different genes, change TC, TG, HDL-C, LDL-C and ApoA1/ApoB among genotypes in the 638 controls at P below 0.0004.
entries.snippet: As shown in Figure 1, the levels of TC, TG, HDL-C, and LDL-C and the ratio of ApoA1/ApoB in the control group were significantly different among the three genotypes of the six SNPs, and the levels of ApoA1 were also significantly different among the three genotypes of five SNPs, except for rs3130685 SNP (p < 0.0004).
entries.anchor: Results, Association Between the SNPs and Serum Lipid Levels in Controls

entries.proposition: Table 4 prints, for rs2222896 AA versus AG on triglyceride, a beta of -0.647 with t -11.274, and a 95 percent interval (-1.053 to -0.741) that does not contain the beta.
entries.anchor: Table 4, TG block, rs2222896 AA to AG

entries.proposition: The only WWOX lipid association printed for rs2278075 in controls is lower HDL-C in the AT genotype (beta -0.312).
The Introduction attributes a WWOX rs2222896 genotype effect on LDL-C in an offspring cohort to Johannsen et al., 2018.
entries.snippet: The correlation between the WWOX rs2222896AA genotype and LDL-C was two times that of the rs2222896AG or rs2222896 GG genotypes (Johannsen et al., 2018).

entries.proposition: Reference 16, the Johannsen 2018 entry, is a case report of a WWOX SDR-domain missense variant with complete loss of WWOX protein in epileptic encephalopathy, not a lipid genetics study.
entries.snippet: A Novel Missense Variant in the SDR Domain of the WWOX Gene Leads to Complete Loss of WWOX Protein with Early-Onset Epileptic Encephalopathy and Severe Developmental Delay.

entries.proposition: The Introduction attributes a WWOX rs2278075 genome-wide association (P 5.0e-9) with CVD to Joseph et al., 2017; reference 17 is an epidemiology review.
entries.snippet: Additionally, the WWOX rs2278075 SNP was associated with CVD (p = 5.0 × 10−9) (Joseph et al., 2017).

entries.proposition: Reference 17 (Joseph 2017) is a review titled 'Reducing the Global Burden of Cardiovascular Disease, Part 1: The Epidemiology and Risk Factors'.
entries.snippet: Reducing the Global Burden of Cardiovascular Disease, Part 1: The Epidemiology and Risk Factors.

entries.proposition: The Discussion cites Saez et al. 2010, the WWOX HDL association paper, for the claim that moderate drinking protects arteries.
entries.snippet: Many studies have reported that minimal or moderate drinking (≤1 drink/day for women, ≤ 1-2 drink/day for men) is beneficial to protect arteries (Saez et al., 2010; Simino et al., 2013; Sferra et al., 2020).

entries.proposition: The paper quotes 1000 Genomes CHB frequencies for rs2278075 of T 22.0 percent and says the Guangxi Han minor alleles are similar to CHB; the paper's own control T frequency is 14.6 percent (186 of 1276 chromosomes), the case groups 21.2 and 22.9 percent.
The authors state that drug effects on lipids in cases cannot be excluded and that lipid-genotype associations could not be examined in the CAD and stroke groups.
entries.snippet: Finally, some CAD and IS patients were taking some drugs that may affect serum lipid profiles. Therefore, we could not determine the association between the SNPs and serum lipid levels in CAD and IS groups.

entries.proposition: Haplotype analysis: the paper prints R-squared for the EHBP1 pair in each group.
entries.snippet: There was strong LD between the EHBP1 rs2710642 and rs10496099 SNPs in the three groups (control, D' = 0.951 or R 2 = 0.821; CAD, D' = 1.000 or R 2 = 0.938; and IS, D' = 1.000 or R 2 = 0.690).
